h: Play, Gardens and the North Norfolk Coast
p: Pensthorpe isn't just for birdwatchers. Families will find plenty for children too, including WildRootz, an adventure play area that encourages kids to climb, build and explore outdoors, and Hootz House, an indoor play space for rainy days. That mix makes it an easy place for grown-ups to enjoy the gardens and lakes while the kids burn off energy. Between the play areas, the lakeside paths and the bird hides, it's a calm, unhurried place for little ones to get properly close to nature.

The gardens deserve a mention of their own. The Millennium Garden was designed by the celebrated Dutch plantsman Piet Oudolf, famous for his naturalistic style of drifts of grasses and perennials, and it's at its showiest in late summer and early autumn. Take a slow loop round the lakes, pause at the hides and keep an eye out for wildfowl. Spring brings fresh growth and birdsong, while autumn and winter can bring flocks of visiting birds.

Fakenham is perfectly placed for exploring. The north Norfolk coast is a short drive away, where Holkham's huge beach and pine woods sit beside a grand Palladian hall and estate. Wells-next-the-Sea, a pretty harbour town, is linked to Walsingham by a narrow-gauge steam line, and the village of Walsingham itself has been a place of pilgrimage for centuries. From Morston or Blakeney, boat trips head out to see the seals at Blakeney Point. Closer to home, the Thursford Collection, near Fakenham, is known for its steam engines and fairground organs, and its Christmas show is a much-loved festive tradition in Norfolk. Fakenham Racecourse also hosts jump meetings through the year.
